accuracy.evidence: Formulae match the Edexcel/AQA/OCR A-level Mathematics specifications (Pure: compound-angle formulae for sin, cos and tan of A ± B, double-angle formulae, exact values, solving equations and proving identities) and the DfE A-level subject content. Every exact value was checked numerically: sin 75° = (√6 + √2)/4 ≈ 0.966, sin 15° = (√6 − √2)/4 ≈ 0.259, cos 105° = (√2 − √6)/4 ≈ −0.259; sign rows checked live at A = 50°, B = 20°; sin 2x = cos x on (0°, 90°) gives only 30°, sin 2x = sin x on (0°, 180°) gives only 60°.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips named in the adult text: splitting over the plus (step 1 myth with sin A + sin B above 1, sorter cards, prediction, challenge 'lin'), sin 2A = 2 sin A (step 5 graph and prediction, p3, m4), plus sign in cos(A + B) (sign-fix step, prediction, m1, m2), B − A for A − B (exact-value step feedback 'Swap the order'), wrong form of cos 2A (p4, challenge 'flip'/'pyth') and dividing by sin x (challenge 'div', m3 hint).

lab_distinct.evidence: New mechanics for trigonometric identities: dragging two rays on a unit circle while bars compare sin(A + B) with sin A + sin B, filling slots so the stacked sin A cos B and cos A sin B segments reach the A + B point, flipping signs in three formulae with a live numeric equality check, composing 15°, 75° and 105° from special-angle tiles and a ± toggle, and picking forms of cos 2A beside sin 2A and 2 sin A curves. Passed the 30% shingle gate against all labs including flagquot and other A-level labs.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers before being told: the myth step shows sin A + sin B overshooting 1 at A + B = 90°, the stack step shows the two products literally adding to the height of the point, the live check shows which sign balances for cosine, and the cos 2A tiles give a counterexample when a myth is tapped. Step summaries state each formula only after the task is complete.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong answers: 'Is sin(A + B) equal to sin A + sin B?' (tempting: yes, by analogy with brackets), 'Is cos(A + B) = cos A cos B + sin A sin B?' (tempting: same pattern as sine), and 'Is sin 2A = 2 sin A?' (tempting: double the angle, double the sine); each is then tested by the task that follows.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with distinct m= messages for each slip: splitting over + or −, the cosine sign, confusing sin 75° with cos 75°, dividing by sin x, the x = 30° check, the half-angle confusion, the tan denominator sign, the sign of 1 − 2sin²x and the cos²x versus cos 2x slip.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py: kid text 0.9 (learner limit 6.5), adult text 8.1 (limit 9.5). Canvas labels are formulae or one short line ('Tap a sign to flip it', 'Drag either dot round the circle'); every paragraph adds one idea with worked numbers.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler regex and the 12% duplicate gate. Kid paragraphs: test the myth with numbers, the true sine rule and the stacking picture, signs and exact values, double angles and choosing a form. The adult text gives the specification link, the unit-circle proof, seven named mistakes and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots of all six steps at 360 px light (android profile), iPhone 13 light and dark, and desktop (shot.cjs): the unit circle and bars, the slots and four product tiles, three sign rows, angle tiles with the ± toggle, the graph and five cos 2A tiles all fit with no clipping after widening the circle and moving the slots apart. Every canvas action is repeated as a button below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all tasks complete with Show me, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark, no console or page errors. Every drag or tap has a button route (A/B ± 15°, tile buttons and remove buttons, one flip button per row, angle and sign buttons, cos 2A buttons). The canvas aria-label restates the current values, slots and results.
